claim: China's share of global iPhone production fell from 83% in 2024 to 74% in 2025, per Smart Analytics Global (SAG) estimates.
stance_target: manufacturing diversification is rapid, not physically slow
quoted_support: Research firm Smart Analytics Global (SAG) estimates that China's share in global iPhone production declined to 74 per cent in 2025 from 83 per cent the previous year, while India's contribution rose sharply from 14 per cent to 23 per cent over the same period.

claim: Counterpoint Research projects India's iPhone assembly share to reach around 26% in 2026, versus an industry estimate/headline figure of 28%.
stance_target: magnitude of 2026 India assembly share -- estimates diverge by provider
quoted_support: Counterpoint Research estimates India's share could increase further to around 26 per cent in 2026, reflecting broader industry expectations that Apple's manufacturing expansion in the country will continue to accelerate.

claim: Over the past five years Apple manufactured iPhones worth nearly $70 billion under India's PLI scheme, with roughly $51 billion (about 73%) exported.
stance_target: India assembly scale and export orientation, distinct from domestic value capture
scope_conditions: India PLI scheme, trailing five years to 2026
quoted_support: Over the past five years, Apple manufactured iPhones worth nearly $70 billion under India's production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme, with exports accounting for approximately $51 billion, or nearly 73 per cent of total production.

claim: Indian suppliers now export components and sub-assemblies (PCB assemblies, mechanical parts) TO China, a reversal of historical flows, reaching a record $2.5 billion in FY26 per commerce ministry data.
stance_target: China remains purely upstream/component-source anchor with no reverse flow
scope_conditions: India-China component trade, FY26, per Indian commerce ministry
quoted_support: Indian suppliers are now exporting components and sub-assemblies such as printed circuit board assemblies and mechanical parts to China, reversing traditional supply chain patterns... exports of such components and sub-assemblies reached a record $2.5 billion in FY26.

claim: Analysts caution China retains 'unmatched scale and operational flexibility' via its deep supplier ecosystem, and India is unlikely to replace China entirely in Apple's supply chain in the near term.
stance_target: assembly-share shift implies component/value-chain shift away from China
quoted_support: China continues to retain major advantages, including a highly developed supplier ecosystem, mature manufacturing infrastructure, skilled labour availability and extensive experience in handling large-scale electronics production. Many of Apple's most critical suppliers and component manufacturers also remain deeply rooted in China.

claim: iPhones accounted for more than 75% of India's smartphone exports in the first 11 months of FY26, roughly Rs 2 trillion of ~Rs 2.6 trillion total smartphone exports.
stance_target: scale of India's iPhone assembly/export base
quoted_support: The first 11 months of FY26 also saw iPhones account for more than 75 per cent of India's smartphone exports, contributing nearly Rs 2 trillion out of total smartphone exports worth around Rs 2.6 trillion.
